sci: Several families, mainly Hylidae and Rhacophoridae
ov: Any frog that spends most of its life in trees. Tree frogs come from several families that are not closely related but have evolved to look alike: usually small and slender, with sticky discs on their finger and toe tips that give them a strong grip.
rg: Hylid tree frogs: Europe, temperate Asia, Australia and the Americas. Shrub frogs: Africa and South and Southeast Asia.
df: Mostly insects and other invertebrates; some larger species eat small vertebrates.
fx: Gliding has evolved separately in several tree frog families, using fully webbed hands and feet and flaps of skin.
Some lay their eggs on leaves over water, so the tadpoles drop into the pond when they hatch.
